subject: physics
question_text: What is inertia? Explain the three types of inertia with one example each.

mark_split.label: Inertia of motion and of direction

verification.note: PREDICTED — Session 89 enumeration sweep (archetype × object grid over the NCERT chapter): this question has not appeared in any paper or source book we hold, but the chapter contains it and the 2-mark/4-mark format admits it. Authored as a lean card; promote to a full card when a paper season or a Telangana IPE teacher validates the cell. Split invented, as everywhere.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: Inertia and inertia of rest
lines: Inertia is the property by which a body
resists any change in its state of rest or
Inertia of rest: a body at rest stays at rest.
Example: when a mat is beaten, the mat moves
away and the dust stays behind and falls.
steps.why: Every example works the same way: one part of the system is forced to change, and the rest keeps doing what it was doing.
common_mistakes: Defining inertia as a force; it is a property of the body, not a force acting on it.

recall.must_convey: That inertia is resistance to a change of state, and inertia of rest keeps a body at rest, as with dust and a beaten mat.
accept: dust stays when the mat is beaten

steps.memory_tip: Inert means not acting by itself. Inertia is that property of a body, never a force.
steps.margin_note: First mark. The definition and the rest example together. Both are needed for it.

steps.label: Inertia of motion and of direction
lines: Inertia of motion: a body in motion keeps
moving. Example: a passenger keeps moving
forward when a bus stops suddenly.
Inertia of direction: a body keeps moving
along the same straight line. Example: mud
leaves a spinning wheel along the tangent.
steps.why: Inertia of direction is the one that needs Newton’s first law in full: "in a straight line" is a separate claim from "keeps moving".
common_mistakes: Giving the same example for inertia of motion and of direction.

recall.must_convey: That inertia of motion keeps a body moving, as a passenger does when a bus stops, and inertia of direction keeps it in a straight line, as mud leaving a wheel.
accept: passenger keeps moving when the bus stops
mud flies off along the tangent
keeps moving in a straight line
reject: dust stays when the mat is beaten

steps.memory_tip: Inertia of motion keeps a body moving; inertia of direction keeps it straight. Bus jerk, then mud off a wheel.
steps.margin_note: Second and third marks. Two types, one mark each, and a DIFFERENT example on each.

steps.label: What it depends on
lines: All three follow from Newton’s first law.

lines.text: Mass is the measure of inertia

lines: The greater the mass, the greater the inertia
steps.why: Naming mass as the measure connects all three types to one number, which is what the last mark is usually for.
common_mistakes: Naming weight as the measure of inertia; weight changes with place, inertia does not.

recall.must_convey: That all three follow from the first law and mass is the measure of inertia.
accept: mass is the measure of inertia
all three follow from the first law
reject: passenger keeps moving when the bus stops

steps.memory_tip: Mass, not weight. On the Moon the same body has the same inertia and less weight.
steps.margin_note: Fourth mark. One word — MASS. The greater-the-mass line completes it.

insider_note: Three types with three different examples are 3 of the 4 marks; mass as the measure of inertia is the fourth.
